I stopped using Postman when it magically started connecting to a central server for nothing useful. A dev tool that should work offline now requires cloud connectivity.
We went with curl, Invoke-WebRequest, HTTP files, Insomnia, after Postman went cloud online and became a forbidden tool on our systems.
Postman is slow, eats a ton of memory, and it becomes more and more restrictive to non-logged-in users.
I liked Postman, preferred the online version, but slowly they pushed users towards the app, making it harder to use without an account, then harder to use the online version at all.
Postman is so incredibly bloated and slow these days. All I want is a REST client, but every basic task requires digging past confusing platform and cloud stuff I have no interest in.
After v9.11.0 I found the Postman process hanging in memory after closing it; after a few days of not using the app it ended up eating 10% of my CPU time.
I also moved on from Postman a while ago; it had become bloated, slow and buggy, and I found urlencoding issues in my particular use case.

After a layoff, deleting a user's Postman workspace also deleted their trash bin, permanently losing our QA environment/test keys even though support restored collections. There's a reason 'no-cloud' is good for these tools.
As soon as Postman asked for a login I uninstalled it and have been curling from text files ever since.

I'm tired of Postman freezing when sending JSONs over a MB in size. I had to purge it from the system a couple times because the tab wouldn't even load on startup, making the whole thing unresponsive.
Postman dug its own grave after selling out itself for VC money.
Be careful with Postman. It seems they upload all your secrets to their servers. We stopped using it a while ago.
I switched to Insomnia when Postman changed their pricing, wanting us to pay like $300 more per month (before they backtracked).
My biggest gripe with Postman is the horrible theming. Except for light and dark, zero control over the appearance of an app I have to look at for hours almost every day.
Postman has become a bloated, enterprisey mess.
Maybe I never appreciated the power of Postman but I never understood why they thought it would be a good idea to charge monthly for a tool that's just a GUI on top of curl.
I've been using Postman for a while now and it's really handy. You can save requests in collections so you can rerun the same requests for testing purposes.
Postman automatically remembers cookies, very very handy — the only extension I've seen that does this.
When putting files in a post request, Postman doesn't remember the files for you. Also there's no way to stop an ongoing request besides resetting and clearing all parameters.

We've been using Postman for a while, it's invaluable for testing/validating APIs across environments, but we've long waited for live collection sharing without needing everyone to export/import JSON files.
